title: International school jobs in Vietnam: pay and requirements
description: What Vietnam's international and bilingual schools require, what they pay in 2026 (housing, flights, tax), when they hire and how ESL teachers move up.
h1: International school jobs in Vietnam: requirements, pay packages and the hiring cycle
intro: International schools in Vietnam hire licensed teachers, not TEFL holders: expect to need a teaching licence such as QTS, a PGCE-based UK qualification or a US state licence, plus two to three years' teaching experience. A 2026 recruitment guide puts premium Ho Chi Minh City schools at about US$2,500-4,000 a month, usually with housing support, flights and medical cover. Bilingual schools ask less and pay less, and the big schools recruit for an August start through group portals and international job boards.
keyPoints: The legal floor at a foreign-invested school is **a university pedagogy degree or equivalent** (Decree 86/2018 Art 38(3)). A TEFL, TESOL or CELTA is not a pedagogy degree, so it does not get you into the classroom on its own.

Premium international schools: about US$2,500-4,000 a month for licensed teachers in recruitment guides, plus housing support, flights and medical cover. Bilingual and private 'international programme' schools advertised US$1,700-3,000 a month in September-October 2026.
The work permit still needs a bachelor's degree plus 2 years' relevant experience (Decree 219/2025). Years taught in Vietnam count only if you held Vietnamese work permits for them.

Large schools hire through Cognita, Nord Anglia and Inspired portals, Schrole, Tes, Search Associates and Teacher Horizons. Get your licence, references and documents ready in September-October for the following August.

'International' in a name is no guarantee: American International School Vietnam [stopped paying staff in 2024](https://vietnamnews.vn/society/1652922/head-of-american-international-school-vietnam-banned-from-leaving-viet-nam.html) and [was dissolved in January 2026](https://tuoitre.vn/nld/american-international-school-officially-dissolved-196260114102410854.htm). Talk to current teachers before you sign.

sections.title: International vs bilingual schools: what is the difference

blocks.text: Ho Chi Minh City has three kinds of employer that foreign teachers mix up. **International schools** teach a foreign curriculum (IB, American, British) to fee-paying students and recruit internationally with full packages. **Bilingual schools** are usually private Vietnamese schools that run English-medium or integrated programmes alongside the national curriculum and pay foreign teachers a monthly salary. Language centres, which most new teachers start in, are covered in [our guide to the types of teaching jobs](/teach-in-vietnam/types-of-english-teaching-jobs-in-vietnam).

eno.vn's [school directory](/schools) lists Ho Chi Minh City's international and bilingual schools among its employers. Teachers who worked or interviewed there can vote and write reviews, which a moderator reads before they appear; most schools have few or no reviews yet, so treat it as a list to research from rather than a ranking you can rely on alone.

blocks.text: Job ads still use the old district names (District 2, District 7, Binh Thanh). Since July 2025 official addresses use new ward names, and the city now includes the former Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau provinces, so check where a campus actually is before you compare offers.

sections.title: What international schools require: licence, degree, experience

blocks.text: What Vietnamese law sets

The rules depend on what kind of school employs you. At general schools licensed as foreign-invested, teachers need at least a university pedagogy (teaching) degree or equivalent, and preschool teachers at least a college-level preschool-pedagogy qualification ([Decree 86/2018, Art 38](https://vcci.com.vn/legal-document/nghi-dinh-862018nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-hop-tac-dau-tu-cua-nuoc-ngoai-trong-linh-vuc-giao-duc)). In practice, international schools satisfy the 'equivalent' with recognised teaching credentials such as PGCE/QTS, a US state licence or home-country certification. **A TEFL certificate is not a pedagogy degree.**

blocks.caption: Legal minimums for foreign teachers by setting (Vietnamese decrees and circulars in force October 2026)
rows: Integrated programme (foreign curriculum combined with Vietnam's)
Degree matching your subject plus a pedagogy certificate; Level 5 (about C1) if you teach in a foreign language
Teaching subjects in English at a Vietnamese school
Level 4 (about B2) for primary and lower secondary, Level 5 (about C1) for upper secondary; exempt with a full-time degree earned abroad in English
College degree plus a 'suitable' teaching certificate (native speakers; non-native speakers also need Level 5 proof unless their degree is in the language)
Bachelor's degree plus 2 years' relevant experience

blocks.text: [Decree 222/2025](https://luatvietnam.vn/linh-vuc-khac/tieu-chuan-giao-vien-day-hoc-bang-tieng-nuoc-ngoai-883-103475-article.html) matters mainly for bilingual schools: it covers subjects such as maths and science taught in English at Vietnamese institutions, and law-firm summaries say it does not apply to wholly foreign programmes at 100%-foreign-invested schools. A native speaker with a degree earned abroad in English is exempt; a non-native teacher without one needs B2 or C1 proof.
What schools ask for in practice

items: **Saigon South International School (SSIS)** normally hires teachers with a master's degree and at least 2 years of successful teaching experience who are certified or licensed in their home country ([SSIS on OpenApply](https://search.openapply.com/schools/saigon-south-international-school)).

**ISHCMC** (part of Cognita, IB programmes) says all its teachers are IB-certified, publishes no numeric minimums on its [careers page](https://www.ishcmc.com/who-we-are/careers/) and takes applications through Cognita Careers.

**SSG Education** (Binh Thanh) asked for a B.Ed, PGCE, QTS or US licence plus 2+ years for primary maths, science and ELA posts starting August 2026 ([the ad](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/primary-mathscience-and-ela-teachers-starting-august-2026)), so even some non-premium schools want a licence.
Across premium schools the working benchmark is a licence plus 2-3 years' experience. Ask each school whether it counts years at a language centre towards that.

blocks.text: The work permit test still applies

Teachers are filed as 'experts': a bachelor's degree or higher plus at least 2 years of relevant work experience ([Decree 219/2025/ND-CP, Art 3(3)(a)](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html), in force since 7 August 2025; the old rule was 3 years). The usual proof is a letter from a past employer abroad; experience in Vietnam counts only through earlier Vietnamese work permits. For experts in education, Art 19(3)(đ) also lists, as an alternative proof, documents showing you meet the qualification standard set by education law; how Ho Chi Minh City applies that to a teacher with under 2 years is not published. Most international schools ask for at least 2 years anyway; if you have less, ask the school which proof it will file and get the answer in writing before you travel.

sections.title: What international and bilingual schools pay (2026)

blocks.text: International schools quote packages, not hourly rates, and most quote in US dollars. No official pay statistics exist; most figures below come from 2026 job ads and recruitment guides (older ones are dated), and the written offer is the only number that counts. For language-centre and public-school rates see [English teacher salary in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-salary-in-vietnam).

blocks.caption: Monthly pay at Ho Chi Minh City schools in job ads and recruitment guides, in the currency quoted (2025-2026)
rows: US$1,900-2,350 a month gross, with compulsory social and health insurance
About US$2,500-4,000 a month plus housing, flights and medical cover

blocks.text: Some private schools advertise in đồng: one 'international school' ad in September 2026 offered up to {{vnd:50000000}} a month, and an expired early-2026 ad offered up to {{vnd:60000000}} a month plus a housing allowance. TEFL Org (August 2026) puts international-school pay at upwards of {{vnd:50000000}} a month after tax ([TEFL Org](https://www.tefl.org/teach-english-abroad/teach-english-in-vietnam/)).
Housing, flights, bonuses and children's tuition

Housing support varies more than any other line. TeachAcrossAsia mostly quotes housing allowances of US$1,200-1,800 a month, but the same page also gives US$400-1,800 and US$400-800, so treat the top figure as a ceiling, not the norm. It puts annual flights at about US$1,000-2,000 a year and an end-of-contract bonus at one month's salary ([TeachAcrossAsia](https://teachacrossasia.com/teaching-locations/teaching-jobs-in-vietnam/)). A 2025 recruiter's ad for a British-curriculum school offered housing in the first year and an allowance after, on a 2-year contract.

To judge an allowance, compare it with real rents. A teacher reported one HCMC international school's housing allowance for single teachers at about {{vnd:20000000}} a month in 2024. The [eno.vn Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index) (10 October 2026) puts the median asking rent for a one-bedroom apartment at {{vnd:10000000}} a month in District 2 and {{vnd:7000000}} in District 7 (Phu My Hung), and for a two-bedroom at {{vnd:20000000}} and {{vnd:15000000}}.

Tuition for your own children is part of some packages, but none of the 2026 ads cited here give terms for it, so ask for it in writing before you accept. If you are moving with a partner or children, also ask what medical cover extends to dependants.
Gross, net and 'tax-free'

items: **'Tax-free' in a recruiter ad normally means the school pays your income tax.** Salaries in Vietnam are taxable; residents pay 5-35% under PIT Law 109/2025/QH15 after a personal deduction of {{vnd:15500000}} a month ([personal income tax for teachers](/teach-in-vietnam/personal-income-tax-for-teachers-in-vietnam)).

Employer-provided housing is taxable only up to 15% of your other taxable income; a cash housing allowance may be fully taxable, so ask how yours is structured ([Vietnam Briefing](https://www.vietnam-briefing.com/doing-business-guide/vietnam/taxation-and-accounting/individual-income-tax)).

On a contract of 12 months or more, social insurance is compulsory: you pay 9.5% (8% pension plus 1.5% health insurance) and the school 20.5%, on salary up to {{vnd:50600000}} a month from 1 July 2026.

A school may pay you in US dollars (Labour Code Art 95(2)), but tax and insurance are worked out in đồng; for social insurance, a foreign-currency salary is converted at a bank rate fixed twice a year. Ask which currency you will be paid in and at what rate.

sections.title: When and where international schools hire

blocks.text: International schools start their year in August, and most posts are filled long before. There is no official calendar and recruitment guides disagree: [Spill.org](https://spill.org/en/blog/the-recruitment-timeline-when-to-apply-for-international-roles) says the best schools fill most posts by January, while TeachAcrossAsia puts Vietnam's peak at February-June. The safe plan is to have your licence, references, recruiter profiles and documents ready by September-October for the following August. Bilingual and private schools also advertise outside the main season: Pathway's primary post, for example, was open until 8 November 2026.

blocks.text: Overseas candidates are usually interviewed on video. Vietnam Australia International School says it interviews them through HR or a hiring manager on Microsoft Teams or Zoom, never charges recruitment, training or entrance fees, never asks you to open an e-wallet, and only emails from @vas.edu.vn ([VAS fraud warning](https://vas.edu.vn/en/news/vietnam-australia-international-school-vas-warning-about-fraudulent-recruitment-information)). Scammers copy real schools' names; [our scams guide](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-job-scams-in-vietnam) lists the signs. You can browse current postings on eno.vn's [jobs page](/jobs-vietnam-expats); eno.vn has not verified the employers behind them, and you should never pay to get a job.

The school is your work-permit sponsor and files for you, but the documents come from you, and they take time to collect from abroad. The full process is in [the work permit guide](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers); this is the outline.

items.title: Authenticate your degree and teaching licence
items.text: Vietnam joined the Apostille Convention with effect from 11 September 2026 (Decree 293/2026/ND-CP): documents from member countries need an apostille, others still need consular legalisation. Germany, Austria and Czechia objected to Vietnam's accession, so their documents still go through legalisation ([HCCH status table](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41)). Thai-issued documents also need legalisation until the Convention takes effect for Thailand on 28 February 2027. Each document then needs a certified Vietnamese translation. See [getting your degree authenticated](/teach-in-vietnam/getting-your-degree-authenticated-for-vietnam).

items.title: Get your criminal record check
items.text: It must be issued no more than 6 months before the school files, so time it to the filing date, not the offer date.

items.title: Get the experience letters
items.text: A dated letter on letterhead from each past employer abroad stating your years of experience, plus copies of any earlier Vietnamese work permits.

items.title: Do the health check in Vietnam
items.text: A foreign health certificate is accepted only under a mutual-recognition agreement, so in practice the check is done after you arrive.

items.title: The school files
items.text: It files 60 to 10 days before your start date with the Department of Home Affairs (Sở Nội vụ), which issues work permits for practically every school in the city ([Decision 6093/QĐ-UBND](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/quyet-dinh-6093-qd-ubnd-tp-ho-chi-minh-2026-cong-bo-danh-muc-thu-tuc-hanh-chinh-sua-doi-bo-sung-448197-d2.html)). The decree allows up to 10 working days for a decision and the city publishes 5. The city's fee is {{vnd:600000}} for a new permit, paid by the employer.

items.title: Sign the contract and start
items.text: A permit lasts up to 2 years and can be extended once by up to 2 years. Your school arranges the rest of your paperwork once your work permit is issued; ask exactly what it covers and what it costs.

blocks.text: Changing school later needs a new work permit, even for the same job, and since Decision 346/QĐ-BNV (24 March 2026) you re-submit your degree and experience proof, so keep the authenticated originals and translations ([EY summary](https://www.ey.com/en_vn/technical/tax/tax-and-law-updates/decision-346-qd-bnv-on-the-amendment-and-supplementation-of-administrative-procedures-for-foreign-employees-working-in-vietnam)). Your employer and the authority have the final word on what goes in the file.

sections.title: Moving from language-centre teaching into an international school

blocks.text: For a teacher coming from a language centre, the gap is the teaching licence, not the English: schools want a licence and school experience, and a TEFL or CELTA does not stand in for either. The wider ladder (CELTA, Delta, examining, management) is in [career paths for English teachers in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-career-path-in-vietnam).

blocks.caption: Routes to a teaching licence while living in Vietnam (UK Department for Education and provider pages, 2025-2026)
rows: Recognised by the UK DfE as equivalent to QTS; completing it confers QTS
About a year of mostly online study with teaching practice; a placement school offering at least 120 days and a mentor; provider sets the fee, no DfE funding
Home-country route (PGCE with QTS, US state licence, etc.)
The licence most international schools list
Depends on your home country's rules and whether training can be done from abroad
An academic postgraduate award; check whether it leads to QTS
E.g. Nottingham's PGCEi has an HCMC venue (see below); ask target schools whether they accept it

blocks.text: The UK government says iQTS training happens where you live and work, with no visit to England required, but to teach in English schools where QTS is a legal requirement you must also complete statutory induction ([GOV.UK on iQTS](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/international-qualified-teacher-status-iqts/introducing-the-international-qualified-teacher-status-iqts-pilot)). The practical hurdle in Ho Chi Minh City is finding a school, usually a bilingual or international one, willing to host the placement, which makes a bilingual-school job a natural stepping stone.

The University of Nottingham runs its PGCEi with a Ho Chi Minh City venue for a fixed fee of £5,767, payable in four instalments, with a compulsory in-person induction in the city listed for 25-28 June 2027 and applications closing 4 May 2027 ([Nottingham PGCEi](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/education/study/pgcei/venues/ho-chi-minh-city.aspx)). Its page does not say whether it leads to QTS. iPGCE sellers market them to international-school applicants, so check with the HR of the schools you want before paying.

items: Keep every Vietnamese work permit: under Decree 219 they are the only way years taught in Vietnam count as experience for your next permit.
Get a signed, dated experience letter from each employer before you leave it, stating your job title, dates and whether you were full-time.
Log your contact hours, age groups and levels taught, with timetables and payslips as evidence; it makes your CV and any later application easier to back up.

sections.title: Before you sign: check the school and the contract

blocks.title: An 'international' name is not a guarantee
blocks.text: American International School Vietnam (Nha Be) had 129 foreign teachers when it stopped paying staff in early 2024: foreign teachers received 70% of January's salary and none of February's, and about 85 teachers resigned ([Viet Nam News](https://vietnamnews.vn/society/1652922/head-of-american-international-school-vietnam-banned-from-leaving-viet-nam.html)). In January 2026 the city dissolved the school and ordered the owner to pay the salaries and insurance owed ([Tuoi Tre](https://tuoitre.vn/nld/american-international-school-officially-dissolved-196260114102410854.htm)). Before you sign, ask current teachers whether pay has been on time, and check the school's accreditation and owner.

items: **Contract length and notice.** Premium schools may offer 2-year contracts (one 2025 recruiter ad for a British-curriculum school did). On a 12-36-month contract you must give 30 days' notice; quitting unlawfully costs half a month's salary plus pay for the notice days you skipped, and usually the completion bonus. See [English teaching contracts](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teaching-contracts-in-vietnam).

**Leave.** The law gives 12 days' paid annual leave after 12 months and 12 public-holiday days from 1 July 2026, plus one traditional New Year day and your own National Day. School holidays are a separate, contractual matter: Pathway, for example, adds a 6-day paid summer break.
**Workload.** Ask for periods, not hours: Pathway's load is 30-34 periods of 35 minutes a week, plus 1-2 Saturday admissions mornings a month.

**Documents and deposits.** A school may not keep your original passport, degree or certificates or take a deposit (Labour Code Art 17); since 10 September 2026 a school that does is fined {{vnd:40000000-50000000}}.
**Final pay.** Everything owed must be settled within 14 working days of the contract ending.

faqs.q: Can I teach at an international school in Vietnam with only a TEFL or CELTA?
faqs.a: Not as a classroom teacher at most international schools. Foreign-invested schools must employ teachers with a pedagogy degree or equivalent, and schools read that as a teaching licence such as QTS or a US state licence. A TEFL or CELTA is still useful for language centres and some bilingual schools.

faqs.q: Is an iPGCE accepted by international schools in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: It depends on the school. An iPGCE is an academic award, so check whether the course leads to QTS; iQTS does confer QTS according to the UK government. Ask the schools you are targeting before you pay for either.

faqs.q: Will I be paid in US dollars?
faqs.a: Possibly. The Labour Code lets employers pay foreign employees in foreign currency, but income tax and social insurance are calculated in đồng at a set exchange rate. Ask which currency, which rate and which date before you sign.

faqs.q: Can I tutor privately or work at a language centre alongside my school job?
faqs.a: Not on your school's permit. Teaching for a second employer needs a separate work permit for that employer, and working without one can mean a fine and deportation. Check whether your contract allows outside work at all.

faqs.q: Do international schools pay more in Ho Chi Minh City than in Hanoi or Da Nang?
faqs.a: One 2026 recruitment guide puts international-school pay at US$2,500-4,000 a month in Ho Chi Minh City, US$2,200-3,500 in Hanoi and US$2,000-3,200 in Da Nang. These are guide estimates, not official figures, so compare actual offers.
